messages:
alex: hitting a weird case with the python async client — when we get a 422 the SDK raises an HTTPError but drops the validation payload, so i can't inspect the detailed errors or do an isinstance check for ValidationError.
maria: can you paste a repro + the response body? :eyes:
alex: here's a tiny repro, async call -> raises
```py
resp = await client.create_resource(data=bad_payload)
# raises HTTPError('422 Unprocessable Entity')
```
and the server returns: `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"validation_error\",\"errors\":[{\"loc\":[\"body\",\"name\"],\"msg\":\"too short\"}]},\"request_id\":\"req_abc123\"}`
jason: yup our HTTPError currently only sets .status_code and .message. We added .raw_body historically but it's getting lost inside the async path (or not surfaced on the public exception type). We should preserve the parsed json as well as raw bytes.
alex: stack trace:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 42, in <module>
    await client.create_resource(...)
redwood.errors.HTTPError: 422 Unprocessable Entity
```
maria: UX ask: i'd like to do `except sdk.ValidationError as e:` or at least `isinstance(e, sdk.ValidationError)` and then `e.errors` -> List[dict]. Right now i have to parse e.raw_body myself.
sylvia: suggestion: add a typed ValidationError class that extends HTTPError and add `ValidationError.from_response(resp, parsed_json)` factory. SDK could detect `error.type == "validation_error"` and raise the subclass, with attributes `.errors` and `.request_id`. That would preserve type checks and make handlers straightforward.
jason: agree. For typing, expose a TypedDict: `ValidationErrorPayload = TypedDict("ValidationErrorPayload", {"errors": List[Dict[str, Any]]})` and set `e.payload: ValidationErrorPayload` on the exception. Keep `.raw_body` as bytes for debug/logging too.
alex: quick note: make sure both async and sync clients behave the same. I saw the sync path kept raw_body but async path wrapped in asyncio.CancelledError somewhere in our middleware and lost it.
maria: i'll add a tiny regression test in the async test suite that asserts `isinstance(exc, ValidationError)` and `exc.errors[0][\"msg\"] == \"too short\"`.
ci-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4123 — title: "python sdk: preserve validation payload and raise ValidationError subclass for 422" (assigned to devex) :white_check_mark:
jason: implementation details: keep the original parsed JSON in `_server_payload` string for backward compat, add a public `.payload` as typed object, and include `.request_id` mapped from `resp.headers.get('x-request-id') or payload.get('request_id')`. For chaining, set `e.__cause__ = original_http_exc` so tracebacks show underlying http context.
sylvia: also consider a convenience helper `sdk.errors.parse_error_payload(bytes) -> dict` used by both clients.
alex: ok thanks — i'll pick this up first pass and open a draft PR. can someone add the test mentioned?
maria: i'll add tests + sample server response fixtures. will also verify error subclassing in both sync and async.
jason: tiny nit: update docs/CHANGELOG about new exception fields and cross-language parity.
alex: awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
